Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?assistant

The worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations is the operation for the vertex with the most outgoing edges, which has a cost equal to the number of its outgoing edges.

* The cost of this operation can be as high as |E|, where |E| is the total number of edges in the graph.
* This is because the vertex with the most outgoing edges is essentially the "hub" of the graph, and the cost of the operation is proportional to the number of edges connected to it.

The average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis is |V|.

* This is because each vertex has an equal number of operations, and the cost of each operation is the number of outgoing edges from that vertex.
* The average cost is therefore the average number of outgoing edges per vertex, which is |V|.
